slides.heading: Heap Sort
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Sorting
slides.narration: Let's solve Heap Sort, a hard sorting problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Build a max-heap in place then repeatedly move the max to the end.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Build a max-heap in place then repeatedly move the max to the end.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Build a max-heap in place, then repeatedly move the maximum to the end and restore the heap.
slides.narration: Build a max-heap in place, then repeatedly move the maximum to the end and restore the heap.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Heap sort → O(n log n), in place
slides.narration: Selection sort finds the max by scanning each time. A heap finds it in log n, giving n log n in place.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Heapify from the last parent down
2. Swap root with the last element
3. Sift down within the shrinking heap
slides.narration: Step by step. First, heapify from the last parent down. Second, swap root with the last element. Third, sift down within the shrinking heap.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We sift down from the last parent to build the heap, then repeatedly swap the root with end and sift the root down within end.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n log n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Build bottom-up, and shrink the heap boundary each step.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Heap sort guarantees n log n with constant memory, but is cache-unfriendly and unstable.
